quote: The fovea is absent in shinks [12, 13], and it is primarily composed of cones to correlate and enhance visual acuity [14].
note: Family-level claim, so g at most. Check it against the measured skink record intake#22 (Tiliqua rugosa fovea): if that record reports a fovea, the family statement is contradicted inside Scincidae and rule 5 blocks using it for Trachylepis. A skink measurement contradicts the family statement: the abstract of a 2012 retina study of Mabuya aurata (doi 10.33899/edusj.2012.59209, now Heremites auratus, once also placed in Trachylepis) reports two foveae, a deep centrodorsal and a shallow dorsotemporal one. So the family statement should not be carried.
